objects.original: The supplied successful stopped-query output q and test index N, the same query count N(Y)+1, actual measurable center Y, its probability law, gradient-square moment and explicit Jensen bound.
objects.reconstructed: The same arbitrary q,N satisfying the finite interpreter equation at all centers; real-cast successful gradient-test count at measurable Y and its expected-work bound.
objects.evidence: The live proximalQuery residual branch returns its current iterate and count one; failed branches recurse and increment successful counts. Private successful_query_unique compares the full returned pairs, so the final successful gradient test is counted. The main proof uses this equality to identify N=M, rather than bounding a distinct existential count.

domains.original: The scoped component permits complete finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel E and any measurable probability space for a measurable input Y. The paper uses Euclidean space and centers produced by its sampler.
domains.reconstructed: The same E typeclasses, an arbitrary measurable alpha with probability measure mu, measurable Y:alpha->E, and natural-valued N.
domains.evidence: No topology or standard-Borel assumption is imposed on alpha. The pushforward mu.map Y lives on Borel E and remains a probability measure. The coordinate-free finite-dimensional extension and arbitrary input probability space are explicit in the candidate assumptions. They are not a construction of the paper repeated-run centers.

quantifiers.original: For any fixed admissible potential and parameters, every supplied pair q,N with the successful interpreter identity at every y obeys the expected bound for every measurable Y with integrable squared gradient.
quantifiers.reconstructed: q,N are universally supplied parameters; hrun is forall y, with fuel and returned count N(y)+1. Y and its square-gradient integrability are supplied; count integrability and inequality follow.
quantifiers.evidence: The target exports no existential replacement count. Successful_query_unique is valid for arbitrary g,eta,eps and any two sufficient fuels from the same initial point; zero fuel cannot succeed. Applied at each y, equality of pairs gives N(y)+1=M(y)+1 and natural cancellation gives equality of functions. Thus all subsequently transported expressions refer to the supplied N.

assumptions.original: Normalized C2 Hessian bounds and kappa>=1; 0<eta<=c<1 and eps>0; exact successful execution for every y; probability mu, measurable Y, and integrable ||grad V(Y)||^2. Count measurability, count integrability and a cost bound are not premises.
assumptions.reconstructed: Exactly those hypotheses, with the actual run written as proximalQuery and all natural counts cast to real in the integrals.
assumptions.evidence: The source D.3 supplies a logarithmic pointwise bound for its stopped routine. Source D.4 first derives D.7; the candidate explicitly extracts only the conditional Jensen step and leaves D.7 open. Its moment assumption therefore marks the remaining interface dependency rather than silently strengthening a claimed full D.4. The hrun premise encodes the exact implementation, not a cost inequality. Measurability and integrability of N follow through equality with the canonical successful witness.

conclusion.original: The actual successful count under Y is integrable and E[N(Y)+1] is bounded by C_c times 1+log(1+sqrt(E||grad V(Y)||^2)/eps), with the displayed exact C_c.
conclusion.reconstructed: Integrable real count N composed with Y plus one, and precisely the same expectation inequality, logarithm, square root and constant.
conclusion.evidence: The parent Jensen proof derives L1 gradient norm from its L2 moment, dominates log(1+g/eps) by g/eps, applies concavity of log on [1,infinity), and uses variance nonnegativity to replace E g by sqrt(E g^2). The parent count is dominated by an integrable logarithmic envelope. The child identifies N and transports both Bochner integrals via integral_map; no proxy-law or total-variation transfer occurs. The pinned source prose describes uniqueness as proof mechanism; it is implemented in the private lemma, not incorrectly claimed as an extra exported conjunct.

scopes.original: A conditional same-implementation/Jensen component of Algorithm D.2, D.3 and the first inequality of the D.4 Jensen step. D.7 and D.8 remain separate.
scopes.reconstructed: Integrability and expectation of the stipulated successful query under a measurable center with integrable squared gradient. No existence of q,N, error guarantee, sampling kernel, convergence or run-total theorem is exported.
scopes.evidence: The live introduction and all authored lesson statements explicitly retain the center moment dependency. The lesson obligations keep run-wide D.7, aggregation of 2J proximal plus 2J direct gradient calls per phase, parameter substitution and D.8 open. The focused test consumes witnesses from an implemented phase for a positive-dimensional two-node center while retaining its hmoment premise; it does not fabricate that missing run-wide estimate.

constant_dependencies.original: C_c=2+(1+log((1-c)^(-1)))/(-log c), depending only on the fixed contraction upper bound c; RHS also depends on eps and the actual squared-gradient moment.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: Exactly the displayed C_c and the same actual-input moment and eps. No additional universal, dimension, condition-number or law-comparison constant is introduced.
constant_dependencies.evidence: 0<eta<=c<1 implies 0<c<1, hence -log c>0 and log((1-c)^(-1))>=0. The execution parent proves this explicit loose coefficient in its pointwise count bound; the Jensen parent carries it unchanged and the child preserves it under pushforward. The paper states an unspecified C_c0; this is a valid explicit coefficient supplied by the local proof, not an asserted source-optimal constant. N+1, rather than N, accounts for the final successful evaluation.

deltas.description: The scoped implementation component extends Euclidean paper centers to finite-dimensional inner-product Borel E and arbitrary measurable probability input spaces. This domain elaboration is disclosed and valid for the same proof.
deltas.evidence: Candidate assumptions and the live typeclasses state the extension; the proof uses no topology on alpha and transports through its actual measurable Y.

deltas.description: This is only the conditional D.3/Jensen component. The integrable actual-center squared-gradient moment is an input; D.7, phase/run aggregation, parameter substitution and D.8 remain unproved here.
deltas.evidence: Source lines 2169-2186 separate the moment and total-work arguments; publication obligations and lesson scope explicitly preserve them.

deltas.description: The local proof supplies the explicit coefficient C_c=2+(1+log((1-c)^(-1)))/(-log c) in place of the paper unspecified C_c0. It includes the final successful gradient evaluation.
deltas.evidence: Execution parent count_bound proves the pointwise coefficient; the Jensen parent and child use the identical coefficient without inflating it or substituting a different count.

The parent constructs a measurable successful count, proves the logarithmic envelope integrable, and proves the expectation bound by log concavity plus the L2-to-L1 moment bound. Equality N=M transfers the witness properties, and integral_map pulls both the count integral and moment integral back under mu.
